scenes.event: Julia meets with her friends Jack and Joe to discuss her decision about changing her name.
scenes.location: A cozy coffee shop with a quiet corner for private conversations
scenes.description: Julia sits at a small table in the back of the coffee shop, surrounded by her notebook, a half-finished latte, and a few sketchbooks. Her laptop is open, displaying a draft of her latest creative project. Jack and Joe, her two closest friends, join her via a video call on her laptop. Jack is animated and playful, while Joe is more reserved and thoughtful. The atmosphere is warm but tense as the conversation turns serious.

characters.gender: female, aged approximately to, 25 years old
characters.description: A young creative writer and artist in the midst of an identity crisis. characters.position: Sitting at the table, holding a pen in one hand and her laptop in the other

characters.name: Jack
characters.gender: male, aged approximately to, 26 years old
characters.description: Julia's best friend since college; Male; Age: 26; Occupation: freelance graphic designer; Personality: playful, supportive, slightly teasing; Values: loyalty, creativity, authenticity; Interests: stand-up comedy, indie music, sketching; Experiences: helped Julia through a difficult breakup in college, collaborated with her on a joint creative project that went viral, has a history of encouraging her to take bold personal and professional risks.
characters.position: Appearing on the laptop screen, leaning forward with a grin

characters.name: Joe
characters.gender: male, aged approximately to, 27 years old
characters.description: A thoughtful and serious-minded friend who offers practical advice and listens deeply; Male; Age: 27; Occupation: Social worker; Personality: Thoughtful, empathetic, cautious; Values: Loyalty, emotional honesty, personal growth; Interests: Reading self-help books, journaling, indie folk music; Experiences: Worked with at-risk youth in underserved communities, helped a close friend through a difficult identity crisis, grew up in a family that valued open communication.
characters.position: Appearing on the laptop screen, sitting in a dimly lit room with a notebook in his lap

actions.action: Sighs and looks at her friends on the laptop screen
actions.dialogue: I’ve been thinking about this for weeks. I feel like my name doesn’t match who I am anymore, but I also worry about how it will change the way people see me.

actions.action: Leans in closer to the camera and grins
actions.dialogue: Well, if it helps, I’ll start calling you ‘Julia the Great’ to make it easier for everyone. Just kidding, but seriously, you deserve to be whoever you want to be.

actions.action: Nods slowly and speaks with a calm tone
actions.dialogue: Changing your name is a big step, but if it aligns with your sense of self, it might be worth it. Just make sure you’re not doing it to please anyone else.

actions.action: Picks up a sketchbook and flips through it
actions.dialogue: This whole time, I’ve been writing and creating under Julia Long. But I feel like the person I’m becoming is someone else entirely. I just don’t know if I can let go of that.
You can always keep the old name in your back pocket. Like a nickname. ‘Long’ could still be your last name if you want to keep it for your family or legal stuff.

actions.action: Looks at Julia with a gentle expression
actions.dialogue: What matters is that you feel like you’re being true to yourself. If your name is holding you back from that, maybe it’s time for a change. Just take your time with it.

actions.action: Smiles faintly and closes her sketchbook
actions.dialogue: Thanks, both of you. I needed to hear that. I’ll think about it more, but it’s comforting to know I have people who get it.

scenes.plot: Julia is at a crossroads about changing her name to better reflect her evolving identity. She shares her concerns with her close friends Jack and Joe, who offer different kinds of support—Jack with humor and light-heartedness, and Joe with thoughtful, serious advice. The conversation helps Julia feel less alone and more empowered to make a decision that aligns with her values and sense of self.
scenes.social_purpose: To explore the protagonist’s internal conflict and decision-making process through a natural dialogue with friends, highlighting her values of authenticity and self-expression.

chunk.text: Julia’s friends support her in her emotional and identity-driven journey, helping her feel more confident about the possibility of reinvention while respecting her sensitivity and introspective nature.
